articles.title: The Mars rovers carry no clocks set to Earth time, so the engineers driving them shifted their entire lives to a 24-hour-39-minute Martian day, and within weeks JPL staff were sleeping during California afternoons, eating breakfast at midnight, and quietly developing a kind of jet lag no human had experienced before.
articles.summary: NASA's Mars rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance, operate on a Martian day, or 'sol,' lasting 24 hours and 39 minutes. These rovers, active in Gale Crater and Jezero respectively, are vital for Martian exploration. Their sophisticated operations, powered by solar panels and managed through thermal cycles, must constantly adapt to the unique extraterrestrial environment, showcasing advanced space technology and engineering resilience.
